bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Choudhary transfers Rs 579 crore flood relief to 8.27 lakh families - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 15, 2026 Bihar CM Choudhary transfers Rs 579 crore flood relief to 8.27 lakh families Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Source: Facebook/Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday transferred Rs 579.23 crore as relief assistance to the bank accounts of 8.27 lakh flood-affected families in the state. Each affected family received Rs 7,000 under the relief assistance scheme, officials said. The funds were transferred during an event in Patna for flood-affected families across 15 districts, they said. According to a statement issued by the Disaster Management Department, around 49.72 lakh people have been affected by floods, with several rivers continuing to swell following torrential rainfall over the past two to three days. Choudhary also directed the district magistrates of the affected districts to prepare detailed reports on the damage caused by the floods ahead of Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan's visit on Wednesday. A central team led by Chouhan will visit Bihar to assess the flood situation. The chief minister reiterated that the state government was making continuous efforts to find a permanent solution to the recurring flood problem in Bihar. India Bihar Cabinet okays Rs 3,516 cr for Son-Falgu river link project, Vishnupad temple development PTI 15 September, 2026 07:47 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 15 (PTI) The Bihar government on Tuesday approved Rs 3,516.05 crore for the Son-Falgu River Linking Project and to develop the Vishnupad Temple complex in Gayaji on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi. It also accorded approval to a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to be signed between the Civil Aviation Ministry, the Airports Authority of India (AAI), and the state government to expand air connectivity in the state under the Centre’s Modified UDAN Scheme. According to the state tourism department’s proposal that has been approved at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the estimated cost of the Vishnupad Temple complex development is Rs 2,520 crore, while the Son-Falgu River Linking Project is likely to cost Rs 996.05 crore. Show Full Article Under the Rs 2,520-crore Vishnupad Temple Complex development plan, the proposed works include development of the temple premises, construction and development of multilevel car parking, an elevated pathway, Manasarovar-Manpur Bridge, ramps, ghats, dormitory and canteen, pedestrian bridge, among others. The project will be implemented by Bihar Rajya Path Vikas Nigam Ltd (BRPNNL), said the tourism department’s proposal. Every year, a large number of Hindus visit the Vishnupad temple during the Pitri Paksha period to perform Pind Daan rituals. “The Vishnupad Temple in Gayaji is an important tourist destination from historical, traditional and religious perspectives. During the Pitrapaksha Mela and throughout the year, large numbers of domestic and foreign devotees/tourists visit the temple for Pind Daan,” it said. Completion of the proposed project will give a new impetus to Gaya’s centuries-old religious, spiritual and cultural traditions, the department said. Under the Rs 996.05-crore Son-Falgu River Linking Project, an intake well is proposed to be built approximately 23 km upstream from Indrapuri Barrage. Through the intake well, the required quantity of water will be drawn from the Sone river and conveyed through an approximately 11-km-long pipeline to the Uttar Koyal Main Canal at a point about 32.77 km away. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Opens 211 Government Degree Colleges in a Single Day - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Bihar Opens 211 Government Degree Colleges in a Single Day 15 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar has created a landmark in higher education by opening 211 government degree colleges in a single day , taking the total number of constituent degree colleges in the state to 483 . The initiative aims to bring higher education closer to students, particularly in rural and underserved areas. Key Points: 211 New Colleges: The Bihar Government opened 211 government degree colleges across 211 blocks that previously did not have a degree college. Total Colleges: With the addition of these institutions, the number of constituent degree colleges in Bihar has increased from 272 to 483 . Block-Level Expansion: Bihar has 534 blocks , and 211 blocks previously lacked a degree college. The expansion seeks to address this geographical gap in higher education. Saat Nischay-3: The initiative has been undertaken under the fourth resolution of Saat Nischay-3 , titled “Unnat Shiksha, Ujjwal Bhavishya” (Advanced Education, Bright Future) . Rural Access to Higher Education: Most of Bihar's earlier constituent colleges were concentrated in district headquarters , creating accessibility challenges for students from rural areas. The new colleges aim to bring degree-level education closer to their homes. Teacher Training: Around 100 teachers are set to receive training at Oxford University , aimed at strengthening teaching quality and academic capacity. Higher Education and Inclusion: The expansion is expected to improve access to higher education for students from rural, economically weaker and educationally underserved communities . Regional Development: Expansion of higher education infrastructure can contribute to human capital development, employability, skill formation and social mobility in Bihar. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar targets drone spraying across 2.85 lakh acres in 2026-27, sanctions Rs 11.81 crore in subsidy
bihar_raw_news.content: English Agri Commodity News All News Representational image Patna: Bihar has set a target of covering 2,85,160 acres under drone-based crop spraying during 2026-27, with the programme being implemented across all 38 districts under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana as part of the state’s Fourth Agriculture Road Map, reported Dainik Bhaskar. The state government has sanctioned Rs 11.81 crore for the programme, which provides subsidised drone spraying of agricultural inputs, including pesticides and liquid fertilisers, to eligible farmers. According to the Agriculture Department, drone spraying has so far been carried out across 24,789 acres in the state, while subsidies amounting to more than Rs 10.13 crore have been approved for farmers. Agriculture Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha said the initiative is aimed at integrating modern technology with conventional farming practices. Drone-based spraying can help farmers cover larger areas in less time while reducing dependence on labour. How farmers can avail the subsidy Farmers registered on the Agriculture Department’s Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) portal can apply online to avail the subsidised drone-spraying service. Under the scheme, a farmer can avail subsidised drone spraying for up to 15 acres per crop season, with a maximum of two spray applications permitted for a crop or season. Farmers can submit separate applications based on their requirements, including pest and disease control, weed management and application of liquid nutrients. The programme covers the drone-based application of agricultural inputs depending on the crop stage and the incidence of pests, diseases and weeds. Eligible inputs include insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers, micronutrients and bio-pesticides. The Agriculture Department has given priority to Integrated Pest Management (IPM), under which chemical pesticides are intended to be used as a last resort. Their application may be undertaken when pest or disease incidence reaches the prescribed economic threshold level. The scheme provides subsidies for drone spraying of bio-pesticides, chemical pesticides, herbicides and liquid nutrients in accordance with the prescribed provisions. The Bihar government has sanctioned Rs 11,81,30,440 for implementation of the drone-spraying programme during 2026-27. The Agriculture Department is implementing the programme across all 38 districts and has urged eligible farmers registered on the DBT portal to apply online to access the subsidised service.

bihar_raw_news.title: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan to visit Bihar on Sep 16 - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan to visit Bihar on Sep 16 ANI | Updated: Sep 15, 2026 16:38 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 15 (ANI): Union Minister for Agriculture Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit Bihar on Wednesday, September 16, to assess the overall flood situation and evaluate the related damage across the state. During the visit, the Union Minister will conduct an extensive aerial survey of various flood-affected areas of the state, interact directly with affected farmers and common people, and review relief and rescue operations in a high-level meeting with senior officials in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary . A team of senior officials from the Union Ministries of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development will also accompany Shivraj Singh during the tour. As per the scheduled programme, Chouhan will reach Patna from Bhopal and conduct an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas of Dighwara and Maner by helicopter from Patna State Hangar at 10:30 AM. Following his arrival at the Hajipur Police Line at 11:00 AM, he will travel by road to Tersia and Saraipur villages. There, he will inspect the damage caused to crops by the floods and interact directly with local farmers. After taking stock of the flood-affected areas, Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit 'Samvad', Chief Minister's Secretariat, at 12:15 PM. He will also participate in an important review meeting on flood disaster management, relief works and assistance to be provided to farmers, with Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and senior officials. Departing from Patna at 1:30 PM, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit Nawabgarhi in Munger at around 2:15 PM. At Nawabgarhi, he will visit the relief camp and will meet flood victims and assess the quality of ongoing relief work. After this, he will travel by road via Bhagalpur to inspect the Kosi-Karaiya embankment in Navgachia. In the evening, he will visit the relief camp at Bhagalpur Polytechnic College to meet the affected families taking shelter there and enquire about their well-being. Shivraj Singh will also meet flood-affected people on the morning of September 17 before leaving for Patna . (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary releases Rs 579.23 cr aid to 8 lakh flood-hit families
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary releases Rs 579.23 cr aid to 8 lakh flood-hit families Story by ANI | Posted by Ashhar Alam | Date 15-09-2026 Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary Patna Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Tuesday inaugurated an ex-gratia relief distribution program at the 'Sankalp' auditorium at the Public Servants' Residence, transferring ₹579.23 crore via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), providing Rs 7,000 per family directly into the bank accounts of 8,27,472 flood-affected families. The ceremony took place at the 'Sankalp' auditorium located at the Chief Minister's residence. During the event, Santosh Kumar Mall, Principal Secretary of the Disaster Management Department, gave a detailed presentation to the Chief Minister regarding the flood-affected areas, relief and rescue operations, and the facilities being provided to the affected people. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister stated that amidst this challenging flood situation, the state government's top priority is to provide immediate relief, assistance, and security to the affected families. The government stands with the flood-affected people with the utmost sensitivity. No shortcomings will be permitted in the relief and rescue operations, he said. He stated that approximately 50 lakh people across 15 districts, 88 blocks, 575 gram panchayats, 2,642 villages, and 136 wards in 21 cities of the state have been affected by the floods. Floodwaters have impacted around 55,000 hectares of land, causing damage to crops. Relief and rescue operations are being carried out rapidly at all levels in the affected areas. The Chief Minister mentioned that over 1,200 community kitchens are operating to provide food to the flood-affected population. Approximately 1.28 crore meals have been served through these kitchens so far. He instructed officials to ensure the continuous provision of food, drinking water, medicines, and other essential amenities to people in the affected areas. According to the Bihar CMO, twenty-one teams from the NDRF and SDRF are actively engaged in relief and rescue operations. He assured that relief and assistance measures would continue until the situation returns to normal, emphasising that the affected people would not be allowed to face any hardship. The Chief Minister announced that a total of ₹579.23 crore has been transferred today via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of 8,27,472 flood-affected families, at a rate of ₹7,000 per family. He directed officials to maintain complete transparency in the process of identification and verification of eligible beneficiaries. If any eligible affected family has been left out of the assistance scheme, they must be included in the relief list within a week; no eligible affected family should be deprived of government relief. He also instructed that recovery and reconstruction work proceed rapidly alongside relief operations, following the theme of "Build Back Better Than Before." He also mentioned that all recovery tasks, including the provision of agricultural input subsidies, road repairs, and other necessary assistance to affected families and farmers, must be completed within one month. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans nine jaggery units in Muzaffarpur to support sugarcane farmers - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings AI Representational Image Muzaffarpur: Sugarcane farmers in Muzaffarpur may soon have a local avenue to process and market their produce, as the Bihar government plans to establish jaggery-making units in the district under its Fourth Agriculture Roadmap, Jagran reported. Muzaffarpur has been selected under the Bihar State Jaggery Industry Promotion Programme, with a proposal to establish nine jaggery production units in the district. The initiative is aimed at providing farmers in areas located away from sugar mills with a local market for their sugarcane while creating an additional source of income. Of the proposed units, six will be allocated under the general category and three under the Scheduled Caste category. A total of nine farmers or entrepreneurs are expected to benefit from the scheme, with financial assistance provided by the government for setting up the units. The programme specifically seeks to support sugarcane growers in non-milling areas by creating local processing facilities, reducing their dependence on sugar mills and markets in other districts. Subsidy of up to 50% Depending on production and crushing capacity, jaggery units can be established at an investment ranging from ₹12 lakh to ₹1 crore. Farmers or entrepreneurs will be eligible for a government subsidy of up to 50% of the project cost under the scheme. The financial support is expected to encourage entrepreneurs to establish jaggery-processing facilities at both small and larger scales. Local processing to reduce transportation difficulties Farmers living far from sugar mills currently face difficulties in disposing of their sugarcane and may have to depend on markets in other areas. The proposed local jaggery units are expected to reduce these challenges by allowing growers to process sugarcane into jaggery and sell the finished product in local markets. The initiative is also expected to create additional income and employment opportunities in rural areas. Production licence mandatory Farmers will have to obtain a production licence before starting a jaggery manufacturing unit. Assistant Cane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said applicants would have to submit their applications to the office of the District Cane Development Officer. Applicants will be required to deposit a ₹2,100 challan for the licence. The application will then be forwarded by the district authorities to the directorate. Farmers will be able to apply for a jaggery unit only after receiving the licence. Online applications underway The online application process for the scheme has already begun. Interested farmers can apply to avail themselves of the benefits. The department expects the expansion of local jaggery production to help increase sugarcane farmers’ incomes while generating new employment opportunities in rural areas.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar floods: Rahul Gandhi urges govt to carry out relief, rescue operations with full promptness
bihar_raw_news.content: PTI File Photo: Rahul Gandhi urges swift relief as devastating Bihar floods affect nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts. New Delhi: In the wake of devastating floods in Bihar, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday urged the government and the administration to carry out relief and rescue operations with full promptness and ensure that essential aid reaches the affected families as soon as possible. The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha also appealed to Congress workers to step forward and provide all possible assistance to the affected people. "The loss of lives due to the devastating floods in Bihar is extremely heartbreaking. I express my deepest condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones in this disaster. My sympathies are with all those affected by this tragedy," Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. "I appeal to Congress workers to step forward and provide all possible assistance to the affected people. At the same time, I expect the government and administration to carry out relief and rescue operations with full promptness and ensure that essential aid reaches the affected families as soon as possible," Gandhi said. bihar_raw_news.title: SJVN CMD Marks Buxar Unit-II Commercial Launch - HIMACHAL HEADLINES
bihar_raw_news.content: NEWS September 15, 2026 admin Bhupender Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, SJVN, inaugurated a program organized at project premises to commemorate significant milestone of commercial operation of Unit-II (660 MW) of 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project (BTPP) in Bihar. Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects), SJVN, was also present on the occasion. Sh. Bhupender Gupta marked the occasion by cutting the ribbon and pressing the ceremonial inauguration button. He also inaugurated the Centralized Control Room of the Project and visited key operational components, including the Ash Dyke, to take stock of operational preparedness and functioning. Addressing Team STPL, Sh. Bhupender Gupta congratulated entire team on the achievement and attributed the milestone to their collective efforts, dedication and teamwork. Highlighting the strategic importance, Sh. Gupta stated that project will play an important role in meeting the energy requirements of Bihar and supporting socio-economic development of the state. He called upon Team STPL to maintain the momentum and focus on safe, efficient and reliable operation of the power plant. Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel were accorded a warm welcome by Sh. Pulak Kumar Mukhopadhyay, Chief Executive Officer, SJVN Thermal Private Limited (STPL), along with senior officials of STPL. On this occasion, Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects) appreciated the commitment and sustained efforts of Team STPL and credited the achievement to strong team spirit of everyone associated with the project. During the visit, Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel also met Sh. Ajay Yadav, Secretary (Energy), Government of Bihar and Smt. Sahila, District Magistrate, Buxar. During the meeting, detailed discussions was held on various issues related to project including land acquisition works, CSR, PSP projects, PPA-related issues, renewable power available with SJVN and potential investment opportunities in Bihar. Underscoring SJVN’s commitment to environmental conservation, Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel also planted saplings at the Project premises. The 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project, located at Chausa in Buxar District, Bihar, has been implemented by SJVN Thermal Private Limited (STPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN.

On attendance, the CM said monitoring mechanisms would be strengthened to ensure students attend college regularly, adding that improved attendance is essential for the wider higher education reforms to succeed. national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today emphasised that self-reliance in defence sector can be achieved through seamless collaboration among the Defence Forces, Research and Development institutions and the industry. He called for greater dialogue, co-development and co-production to accelerate technology adoption and strengthen India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Addressing the DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, ‘VIMARSH 2026’ in New Delhi, Mr Singh said that DRDO has demonstrated its capabilities in every field, from missiles to radars, combat aircraft to submarines, electronic warfare system to Artificial Intelligence. The Defence Minister said that the reforms witnessed in the defence sector over the past few years are unprecedented and several game-changing decisions have also been taken. These include the Positive Indigenisation List, the Make in India initiative, iDEX, ADITI and the decision to allocate 25 percent of the Defence Research and Development budget to the private sector. Mr Singh asserted that these measures have been taken to ensure that India does not remain dependent on imports in the defence sector, but moves towards self-reliance. Describing MSMEs as a backbone of the Indian economy, Mr Singh said that their contribution in components, sub-systems and essential services is significant in the defence sector. He added that MSMEs will have to continuously focus on quality, delivery, innovation and global standards, as well as increase partnerships with large companies. The Defence Minister stressed that a new wave of defence startups is rising in India. He said that these startups are not only innovative but also agile and are disrupting the traditional defence manufacturing model. The Minister said that the opportunities in the defence sector have increased for them with funding, mentorship, and market access.

national_raw_news.title: 36 mins ago | National 217 India committed to promoting circular economy as part of sustainable development, says Environmen...
national_raw_news.content: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav underlined India’s commitment to embedding circular economy principles into its sustainable development framework. The Minister stressed that India has modernized it’s deep rooted ancient cultural practices of reuse, repair, and conservation values into contemporary policies under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Addressing the inaugural session of the 10th edition of World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026, at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar today, the Minister emphasised initiatives such as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations and Mission life as crucial steps in its circularity journey. Highlighting global collaborations like the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, India-EU joint framework, and Mission LiFE, the Minister stated that circularity must begin at home. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel inaugurated the forum which is being held for the first time in India. Addressing the Forum, the Chief Minister stressed that growth, ecology, prosperity, and sustainability must go hand in hand, framing circular economy principles as the core of India’s sustainable trajectory. Over 2,000 stakeholders from more than 65 countries are taking part in the forum which is being held under the theme ‘Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity,’. As of August 2026, over 83,000 producers and 4,802 recyclers are registered under EPR, processing nearly 482.24 lakh metric tonnes of waste. The global event is jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Central Pollution Control Board, Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, and the Government of Gujarat. Over the two days, the forum will host 4 plenary sessions and 16 thematic sessions covering key areas such as the application of AI, green energy, sustainable finance, governance, and the start-up ecosystem. This will be followed by 80 accelerator sessions hosted globally on September 17th and 18th. Additionally, an international expo featuring over 125 exhibitors will showcase innovative, practical solutions for circular business models. Speaking at the inaugural session, Ambassador of Finland to India, Mikko Kivikoski, said that circular economy is not just an environmental agenda which is limited to West management. He stressed that emerging economies like India has a pivotal role in strengthening the circular economy framework.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 96 National Engineers’ Day marks birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna M Visvesvaraya
national_raw_news.content: National Engineers’ Day is being celebrated today to honor the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, one of India’s greatest engineers. The day is celebrated every year on 15th September to remember Visvesvaraya’s contributions and honour the role of engineers in the nation’s growth. Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to M Visvesvaraya on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, the Vice-President said that M Visvesvaraya was a legendary engineer and visionary nation-builder whose contributions continue to inspire generations. Mr Radhakrishnan said that engineers drive India’s progress through innovation, technology and transformative solutions that advance the lives of people and the nation. He wished that the country’s engineers continue to innovate and build a stronger, more prosperous Viksit Bharat. Mr Modi said that M. Visvesvaraya was an engineering genius whose nation-building vision continues to inspire citizens. The Prime Minister extended his greetings to engineers for their contributions to building, innovating, and providing solutions for a better tomorrow. In a social media post, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that M Visvesvaraya’s life remains an enduring example of excellence, discipline, innovation and public service. Mr Singh added that his extraordinary contribution to India’s nation-building journey will always be remembered. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that M Visvesvaraya’s remarkable contributions played a crucial role in nation-building. Extending greetings to engineers, the Home Minister said that their relentless innovations drive India’s progress through perpetual growth.

national_raw_news.title: Ministry of Law and Justice organises officer-level awareness workshop on Tele-Law ... - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Law and Justice organises officer-level awareness workshop on Tele-Law services under DISHA 2.0 Scheme Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Ministry of Law and Justice organises officer-level awareness workshop on Tele-Law services under DISHA 2.0 Scheme ANI | Updated: Sep 15, 2026 19:53 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 15 (ANI): The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised an Officer-Level Awareness Workshop under the Tele-Law Initiative of the DISHA 2.0 (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice) Scheme at the Mini Secretariat, Nuh, Haryana, on Tuesday. According to the Ministry of Law and Justice, the workshop was chaired by Suresh Kumar, Joint Secretary, Department of Justice and SDM of Nuh, Kunwar Aditya Vikram, CSC Vice President, along with other representatives of the Common Services Centres (CSCs), Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), Panel Lawyers, Nyaya Sahayaks and other key stakeholders working towards strengthening access to Justice at the grassroots level. A total of 150 participants attended the Awareness Workshop. The Awareness Workshop was organised with the objective of enhancing awareness about the Tele-Law programme, promoting the use of technology-enabled legal services, and strengthening coordination among stakeholders involved in the delivery of legal assistance to citizens, particularly those residing in rural and underserved areas. The programme commenced with an inaugural session comprising opening remarks by the Chair, Joint Secretary, Department of Justice. This was followed by a presentation on the DISHA 2.0 Scheme, highlighting its vision of advancing access to Justice through the integrated implementation of Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme (LLLAP), and VIDHI-Sanjeevani. During the technical session, participants were briefed on the functioning and impact of the Tele-Law Services, the role of Common Services Centres (CSCs) as grassroots access points for legal assistance, and the contribution of Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) in facilitating legal consultations for citizens. The session also emphasised the importance of leveraging digital platforms to bridge the gap between legal service providers and beneficiaries, the Ministry said. (ANI) A live demonstration of the Tele-Law Portal and the Nyaya Setu AI-enabled chatbot was conducted to familiarise participants with the digital tools available under the scheme and to showcase how citizens can access legal information and advice through technology-driven platforms. The Awareness workshop concluded with an interactive stakeholder discussion focusing on implementation challenges, best practices, and opportunities for expanding the reach of legal services. Participants also shared suggestions and raised queries regarding the effective delivery of Tele-Law services in their respective jurisdictions. The workshop concluded with a vote of thanks by Gaurav Kumar Tripathi, Under Secretary, Department of Justice, reaffirming the collective commitment of all stakeholders towards strengthening access to justice and promoting legal empowerment across the country. national_raw_news.title: Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India ANI | Updated: Sep 15, 2026 10:40 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 15 (ANI): In a major step towards taking pension awareness and retirement security to rural households, the Department of Rural Development (DoRD) and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to create and support a community-based outreach mechanism of ‘Pension Sakhis’ across rural India. According to the Ministry of Rural Development, the MoU was signed between Amit Shukla, Joint Secretary, DoRD, and Sumeet Kaur Kapoor, Executive Director, PFRDA, in the presence of Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development. The partnership seeks to leverage the extensive community institutional network created under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana: National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), including its Banking Correspondent (BC) Sakhis and other trained community resource persons, to take pension awareness, financial literacy, enrolment and post-enrolment support closer to rural households. The initiative will seek to use the strength of the women-led SHG institutional architecture to address a fundamental challenge in pension coverage: reaching households that may have limited access to formal financial advice and retirement-planning services. Under the partnership, Pension Sakhis will act as trusted community-level facilitators, particularly reaching SHG members, rural women, Lakhpati Didis and other rural participants. They will support households with information on pension and retirement planning, facilitate enrolment, and provide assistance in understanding pension-related services. Speaking on the occasion, Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, said that rural households participating in the SHG movement have distinctive savings patterns, livelihood cycles and risk profiles, and that social security must therefore become an important part of the Mission’s larger objective of sustainable prosperity. He emphasised that “social security is not only about protection against vulnerability; it is also about giving households the confidence and resilience to pursue sustained economic advancement.” Kansal stressed that pension awareness and financial literacy must be built on honesty, transparency and trust. He further highlighted the importance of ensuring that rural citizens receive clear and transparent information so that they can make informed choices about their long-term financial security. Mamta Shankar highlighted the growing importance of retirement planning in the context of rising life expectancy and changing demographic patterns. She expressed the hope that the partnership would substantially improve awareness and adoption of pension products, including the National Pension System (NPS), among rural households that remain outside formal retirement and social-security mechanisms. The collaboration will also strengthen monitoring of outreach and enrolment through digital dashboards and mobile- and web-based solutions, including the Department’s own LoKoS system, enabling the participating institutions to track progress and identify gaps in coverage. Community-level outreach will be supported by appropriate digital systems for monitoring and service delivery. The MoU brings together two complementary strengths: PFRDA’s expertise in pension regulation and retirement-security systems and DAY-NRLM’s unparalleled community reach through women’s collectives...

national_raw_news.title: PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum Advertisment Breaking News Jammu and Kashmir News PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum RK News 15 Sep 2026 07:28 IST Follow Us Chennai, Sep 14: A 13 member media delegation from Jammu and Kashmir, organised by Press Information Bureau (PIB), Srinagar, visited Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum at Muttukadu, Tamil Nadu, on Monday as part of press tour being conducted by PIB Srinagar from Sep 13 to 19. The delegation was briefed about the museum and its heritage structures by curator Lakuma Chebrolu. She explained the architectural features of the traditional homes preserved at the museum and provided information about the different regional styles represented there. The museum houses reconstructed traditional heritage homes from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala. The delegation was informed that the houses were carefully dismantled and reconstructed at the site with the involvement of regional artisans and traditional master builders. The visiting media delegation also explored the traditional streetscapes and living environments recreated at the museum, providing an insight into the architectural and cultural traditions of the southern states. Sharath Nambiar, Director, Dakshina Chitra, interacted with the delegation and briefed them about the history of the museum and its role in preserving India's tangible and intangible cultural heritage. He also highlighted the support extended by the Government, particularly the Ministry of Culture, which provided land for the institution and continues to extend assistance from time to time. The visit provided the media delegation an opportunity to understand the preservation and presentation of traditional architecture, indigenous crafts and performing arts, and their relevance for contemporary audiences. Later the delegation also met Sanjay Ghosh, Deputy Director, CBFC Chennai. The delegation is led by Shahid Mohammad Lone, Field Publicity Officer (FPO), Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), serving as the Conducting Officer, with Ifham Ul Islam Information Assistant, PIB Srinagar accompanying the delegation. The media tour of Srinagar based journalists is also significant since Jammu and Kashmir and Tamil Nadu are states paired together under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB). Daily Excelsior 04:18 AM Sep 15, 2026 IST Journalists from Jammu posing for a group photograph during their Bhopal tour on Monday. Excelsior Correspondent BHOPAL, Sept 14: A 10-member media delegation from Jammu began a press tour of Madhya Pradesh with visits to two of the state's important archaeological and cultural heritage sites, the historic Siva Temple at Bhojpur and the prehistoric rock shelters of Bhimbetka. On the first day of the tour, the journalists visited the Siva Temple at Bhojpur, where they were briefed by officials accompanying the delegation on the history and architectural significance of the monument. Advertisement The delegation was also briefed on the temple's unique architectural features, including its massive stone construction and the scale of the structure. Officials explained the historical importance of the site and efforts to preserve the monument as part of the region's archaeological heritage. The journalists later proceeded to Bhimbetka, one of India's most important prehistoric archaeological sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Officials explained that the archaeological evidence at Bhimbetka spans a very long period of human history, with the site offering insights into the development of human culture and artistic expression. The delegation's visit to both sites provided the journalists with an opportunity to understand Madhya Pradesh's rich archaeological heritage beyond written accounts and photographs. The tour has been organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, to provide journalists with an opportunity to experience the cultural, historical and developmental landscape of Madhya Pradesh firsthand. national_raw_news.title: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru Advertisment Breaking News City SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru RK News 14 Sep 2026 07:30 IST Follow Us Srinagar, Sep 13: In a landmark achievement for SKUAST‑K, Bushra Naaz, PhD scholar under the mentorship of Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head, KVK, Ganderbal has been declared a winner at the National Bio Entrepreneurship Competition (NBEC) 2026, held in Bengaluru. The 2026 edition received an overwhelming response, with over 3,200 registrations from 34 States and Union Territories, making it one of the most competitive national platforms for science-driven entrepreneurship. After successive rounds of screening, mentoring, pitching, and evaluation on parameters such as scientific validity, novelty, feasibility, business potential, team strength, and clarity of articulation, only the most promising student advanced to the Grand Finale. Her pioneering research on plant-based meat analogues stood out for its scientific depth, translational potential, and entrepreneurial promise. In recognition of this breakthrough, Bushra Naaz received a ₹1 lakh award, presented in the presence of Dr. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon, and other eminent figures from India’s biotechnology ecosystem. Reflecting on the achievement, Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head KVK, Ganderbal and Major Advisor to Bushra Naaz, remarked. The recognition of this work is deeply gratifying. For over a decade, I have been engaged with the scientific potential of fava bean, and it is inspiring to see this line of research now being advanced by my student into an innovative solution with societal and commercial relevance. Vice Chancellor SKUAST-K Prof. Nazir Ahmad Ganai congratulated both Bushra Naaz and Dr. Ajaz Malik, stating: This achievement is a proud moment for SKUAST‑K and aligns with our vision to be counted among the top universities in the country. It exemplifies how our scholars and faculty are not only contributing to academic excellence but also translating research into innovation and entrepreneurship. Such recognitions strengthen our resolve to position SKUAST‑K at the forefront of national and global scientific leadership. Read More Subscribe to our Newsletter!
